title: Creator footage supply foundation + single Analyse Endgame
summary: YTIntel keeps the v0.37.3 single-video Analyse focus and adds the first working foundation for the GTA 6 creator-footage supply network inside Vault rather than cluttering Analyse. Creator Assets can index self-recorded or permission-cleared clips, search and rank footage against the currently analysed video, maintain a GTA 6 launch capture board, generate creator-specific attribution/referral links, export the footage manifest, and bridge Make It Yours directly into the footage workspace. Compare remains parked. The rights gate is fail-closed: unknown or restricted footage is never presented as cleared for redistribution.
discord_changes: CREATOR ASSETS FOUNDATION: Vault now contains the first working creator-footage supply workspace for clean gameplay/B-roll instead of adding more clutter to Analyse.

GTA 6 LAUNCH BOARD: a persistent capture checklist covers walkthroughs, missions, driving, police chases, locations, vehicles, businesses, scenic B-roll, long background sessions, online content and update footage.
DISTRIBUTION LOOP: footage records carry a rights status, attribution requirement and creator referral link so free footage can become measurable funnel traffic back into YTIntel.
changes: Added Creator Assets inside the Compounding Vault, keeping the top-level product focused on Analyse, Vault and Watchtower while Compare remains removed.
Added a searchable footage manifest with clip title, game/source, scene/use case, tags, duration, resolution, hosted URL, rights status, attribution rule and notes.
Added source-aware footage matching: the currently analysed video's title and transcript generate search intents, and indexed clips receive a match score against those terms.
Added a strict rights gate: only self-recorded or permission-cleared clips are counted as distributable; unknown and restricted clips remain reference-only.

Added a persistent GTA 6 launch capture board covering full no-commentary walkthroughs, individual missions, city driving, night/rain footage, walking, police chases, aerial footage, vehicles, weapons, interiors, NPC moments, landmarks, cinematic B-roll, fails, long background sessions, online activities, update footage and rare events.
Added creator attribution/referral generation using per-creator links so footage-driven traffic can later be measured and rewarded.
Added JSON manifest export and Markdown capture-board export for moving the footage dataset into storage, automation or another production tool later.
Added a Make It Yours bridge that sends the current analysis into Creator Assets with source-specific footage searches ready.

Preserved the v0.37.3 Analyse repairs: one compact progress popup, folded Activity, source-only Strip, Blake-style short summary, receipt-backed takeaways, Monday-brief re-hooks/payoffs/replay handling, package banking, channel zero suppression, Creator-DNA build sheet, hidden raw Vault entry and AI-ready Markdown export.
Preserved Compare removal on desktop/mobile and from the active Vault UI.
known_limitations: Creator Assets v0.37.4 indexes metadata plus hosted-file URLs in local browser storage. Large video-file upload, object storage, transcoding, CDN delivery and cross-device cloud sync for footage are not implemented yet.
The referral builder creates trackable URL structure, but server-side attribution analytics, creator dashboards, payouts and affiliate accounting are not implemented yet.

Game-publisher/platform rights still govern redistribution. YTIntel deliberately does not treat a gameplay recording as automatically sublicensable; commercial licensing language must be verified before public rollout.
YouTube does not expose a reliable Most Replayed curve for every video. Missing replay evidence remains missing rather than fabricated.
Public storyboard sprites are sampled seek-bar evidence rather than every encoded frame. Exact encoded-frame-by-frame semantic analysis remains an active Endgame workstream.
Automatic visual composition and edit-type classification remain strongest when the optional on-device vision model is ready.
Waveform-level silence/transient analysis requires a directly decodable public audio stream; semantic music/SFX labels additionally require supported source metadata or local audio intelligence.
Watchtower velocity still depends on repeated snapshots; a newly added competitor has no historical velocity until it has been observed more than once.
why_it_matters: The creator-footage idea becomes useful when it is not a random download folder. v0.37.4 starts the compounding loop: YTIntel understands the video to make, turns that into footage demand, matches the demand against a rights-aware gameplay library, and creates attribution that can send creators back into YTIntel. The next infrastructure milestone is moving this local manifest into real object storage, automatic clip ingestion/tagging and measurable creator attribution.
